newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-$0.50 higher-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-$0.50 higher-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Monday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, buoyed by firm packer demand following higher pork prices late last week, livestock dealers said.
The higher pork values eased deficits in packer operating margins, although margins remained in the red, they said.
Several hog buyers said packers were still cutting back on slaughter, but not as drastically as last week.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country and $57.50 to $58.50 at plants, the dealers said.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 higher at $57.00 to $57.50 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants, possibly $59.00 at plants paying premiums for top quality hogs, they said.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 higher at $55.50 to $56.00 in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold fully steady at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants, the dealers said.
Direct cash hog prices in the Midwest were seen further supported by light marketings, they said.
"I don't think we'll be overrun with numbers," an Indiana livestock dealer said.
